title: Reverse an array
statement:
Given an array arr of n elements. The task is to reverse the given array. The reversal of array should be inplace.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: n=5, arr = [1,2,3,4,5]
Output: [5,4,3,2,1]
Explanation: The reverse of the array [1,2,3,4,5] is [5,4,3,2,1]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: n=6, arr = [1,2,1,1,5,1]
Output: [1,5,1,1,2,1]
Explanation: The reverse of the array [1,2,1,1,5,1] is [1,5,1,1,2,1].
```

peerSolutions.title: Python slice assignment keeps the original list object
peerSolutions.author: Rahul Patel
peerSolutions.content:
Python can make a reversed copy with `arr[::-1]`. Slice assignment puts that copy back into the same list, so the array is changed in place instead of making the method return a new list.

This also handles repeated values without any special logic. For an empty list, both slices are empty and nothing changes.

```python
class Solution:
    def reverse(self, arr: list, n: int) -> None:
        arr[:] = arr[::-1]
```

The temporary reversed list takes extra memory. The `n` argument is not needed for the slice operation, but it is kept because it is part of the platform method signature.

Time complexity: `O(n)`.
Space complexity: `O(n)` for the reversed copy.

peerSolutions.title: Recursive solution for reversing list
peerSolutions.author: Avaneesh Srivastava
peerSolutions.content:
## Intuition
To create a recursive approach we need to first understand that step by step we will swap first and last element in the list, so we need to keep track of start index and end index and when start index >= end index the recursion ends.

## Approach
Since the function only has 2 arguments: one is the list (arr) and the other is it's length (n), we will calculate start index to be length(arr)-n and and swap element at start and end index until our base condition is met. We will reduce n by 1 every recursive call. 

## Solution
```python[]
class Solution:
    def reverse(self, arr: list, n: int) -> None:
        start = len(arr)-n
        if start>=n:
            return
        arr[start], arr[n-1] = arr[n-1], arr[start]
        self.reverse(arr, n-1)

```

## Complexity
**Time Complexity:** 
O(n/2)

**Space Complexity:**
Inplace O(n)
